family.description: This entry includes small conductance mechanosensitive channels (MscS), which assembles to a homoheptameric complex [[cite:PUB00019883],[cite:PUB00019884],[cite:PUB00019885],[cite:PUB00101036],[cite:PUB00062568],[cite:PUB00101037]]. Each monomer consists of a N-terminal transmembrane region and a large cytoplasmic segment composed of a five-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet (middle/second) domain and a C-terminal alpha/beta-domain [[cite:PUB00101036],[cite:PUB00062568],[cite:PUB00101037],[cite:PUB00064132]]. This is the beta domain which adopts a Sm-like barrel structure.
family.name: Mechanosensitive ion channel, beta-domain

history.description: Inspected Koprowski 2011 patch Methods, Results, Discussion and Figures 4/6; Rowe 2014 Methods, G168D Results and Figure 4D/E; verified P0C0S1 sequence and PF00924 interval. Three graphs retain six directly observed current or availability effects, with salt bridges, disulfide locking and cage compression kept interpretive. Structural domain boundaries and assay-specific buffers, voltages, genotypes and pressure protocols remain separate. Minimal caches and unresolved coverage accompany an IN_PROGRESS overlay; schema validation passed. Partial curation is not family completion or independent endorsement.

history.description: Saved current-content review 20261011T081606Z-pf00924-mscs-interface-redox-and-crowding with digest 2b38e2b5431bff1e3a8f9393d9322115d5871a1d321a4a1c6cf6558cf752dc9e. causal_graphs.context: pTRCMscS variants; bath 400 mM sucrose, 200 mM KCl, 90 mM MgCl2, 4 mM CaCl2, 5 mM HEPES at pH 7.2. Pipette solution omits sucrose; pipette voltage is +15 mV. Pressure steps are separated by at least 3 min. Figure 4 displays three pressure responses from the same patch per genotype, not three independent replicates.

evidence.explanation: Figure 4 WT and G168D recordings and the beta-domain Results show the loss of visible decline. Discussion explicitly limits separation of desensitization and inactivation.
Maps both altered reference residues within the profile interval while preserving the distinct structural TM3b/beta assignments.

edges.mechanism: G168D traces retain activity during maintained pressure where WT traces decline. The edge encodes the directly observed channel-current behavior without assigning a unique hidden gating state or atomic explanation.
edges.subject: mscs-g168d-substitution

evidence.explanation: Figure 4 compares the double mutant with both singles and WT. The double-mutant electrical phenotype is adopted; its structural salt-bridge cartoon is not labeled observed.

edges.mechanism: The N117K/G168D double mutant regains WT-like current decline compared with G168D. This context-specific restoration is not an activating effect of N117K alone or direct proof of a compensating salt bridge.
edges.subject: mscs-n117k-added-to-g168d

causal_graphs.family_mapping: UniProtKB:P0C0S1, mscS/yggB/b2924/JW2891, is a 286-residue K-12 reference, sequence version 1. Exact UniProt/InterPro agreement places PF00924 at 114-180, including N117 and G168. The paper's structural beta domain is 128-181 and places N117 in TM3b. HMM and structural boundaries must not be conflated; complete experimental clone junctions remain unverified.
causal_graphs.limitations: The 2011 protocol does not distinguish desensitization from inactivation. No direct salt-bridge formation or interdomain motion is measured; cartoons are interpretations. Pressure levels differ among traces and no exact common-pressure rate is claimed. Temperature, patch-specific induction and independent replication are not established by the adopted panels.

nodes.label: G168D replacing WT MscS in pressure-clamp assays
N117K added to the G168D full-length channel
Decline of MscS current during sustained pressure

causal_graphs.scope: Full-length E. coli MscS variants in inside-out membrane patches from MJF465 lacking mscK, mscS and mscL; adopted endpoint is current decline during sustained pressure, not an isolated beta-domain activity.
causal_graphs.title: G168D impairs MscS current adaptation and N117K restores it in the double mutant

causal_graphs.context: Figure 6B inside-out patches with the 2011 pH 7.2 bath and +15 mV pipette protocol. Control, 2.5 mM DTT and washout are compared at the illustrated pressure steps; MscL openings remain a pressure-response control. Single-cysteine channels are active in Figure 6A, but its caption does not assign their individual patches to a strain.

evidence.explanation: Figure 6B control and DTT traces show the reversible appearance of MscS activity; MscL is retained in the MJF429 background.

edges.mechanism: DTT restores detected MscS openings in the double-mutant preparation where nonreducing control pressures above the MscL threshold fail to open detectable MscS channels. The measured electrical response is retained without a direct bond-cleavage arrow.
edges.subject: dtt-in-double-cysteine-assay

evidence.explanation: Figure 6B washout trace and caption establish loss of MscS activity after DTT removal. The accompanying S-S cartoon remains interpretive.

edges.mechanism: Removing DTT after the reducing condition eliminates detected MscS activity while MscL openings persist. This reversibility is part of the observed assay, not proof of one uniquely identified nonconducting conformation.
edges.subject: dtt-washout-double-cysteine

causal_graphs.family_mapping: P0C0S1 reference N117 and G168 both lie in PF00924 residues 114-180. N117 belongs structurally to TM3b and G168 to the beta domain. Native full-length channel mutations, not a truncated-domain reconstitution, underlie these comparisons.
causal_graphs.limitations: Reversible reducing-agent dependence supports a redox-sensitive constraint but does not itself measure an S-S bond or distinguish closed from inactivated states. Complete construct sequence, temperature, independent replicate counts and folding controls are unresolved. No universal redox regulation of WT MscS is inferred.

nodes.label: Addition of 2.5 mM DTT to N117C/G168C pressure assay
DTT washout after the reducing condition

causal_graphs.scope: Full-length N117C/G168C MscS in MJF429, which lacks mscK and mscS but retains MscL. The endpoint is detectable MscS channel activity, not a directly measured disulfide reaction.
causal_graphs.title: DTT reversibly restores pressure-evoked N117C/G168C MscS activity

causal_graphs.context: pB10b expression; Methods name MJF465 and PB113, with retained MscL in PB113 used for mutant midpoint calibration, but do not assign each Figure 4 patch to one strain. Inside-out bath has 400 mM sucrose, 200 mM KCl, 50 mM MgCl2, 5 mM CaCl2, 5 mM HEPES at pH 7.4; pipette potential 30 mV. Cytoplasmic Ficoll 400 is 5% w/v, n=3 patches per genotype, with a 10-second conditioning tension between test pulses.

evidence.explanation: Figure 4D and its caption quantify increased WT inactivation at 5% Ficoll. No complete-inactivation claim at every tension is adopted, and the separate 10% panel-A example is not substituted for this comparison.

edges.mechanism: Adding cytoplasmic 5% Ficoll increases the unavailable WT fraction under the conditioning-tension protocol relative to no-Ficoll WT. Crowder and mechanical history form a joint context; the initially activatable population remains available before conditioning.
edges.subject: wt-ficoll-conditioning-system

evidence.explanation: Figure 4D/E and the associated Results support the mutant-versus-WT comparison at 5% Ficoll. No 2011 voltage, buffer or unresolved adaptation-state label is imported into this later experiment.

edges.mechanism: Under the 5% Ficoll and conditioning-tension protocol, G168D retains a larger available channel fraction than WT. This is relative resistance to inactivation, not an absolute inability to inactivate or proof of cage compression as the sole cause.
edges.subject: g168d-ficoll-conditioning-replacement

causal_graphs.family_mapping: G168D changes the reference glycine within P0C0S1 PF00924 residues 114-180. The intact channel, membrane and controlled mechanical perturbation are the tested system, not isolated beta-domain sufficiency. Full pB10b clone sequence is not independently reconstructed.
causal_graphs.limitations: Inactivation is operationally measured through the decreased channel population available at the second test pulse. Tension is required; Ficoll alone is not assigned a sufficient cause. Pressure-to-tension conversion uses reference midpoints and a constant-curvature assumption. Cage compression, salt bridges and specific atomic trajectories are not directly observed. Panels A/B use 10% Ficoll and must not be substituted for the D/E conditions.

G168D replacing WT in the Ficoll-plus-tension assay
Channel fraction unavailable at the second test pulse

causal_graphs.scope: Figure 4D/E of the 2014 study, using full-length WT and G168D MscS and pulse-step-pulse availability measurements. This is distinct from the 2011 sustained-pressure adaptation protocol.
causal_graphs.title: Cytoplasmic Ficoll promotes tension-conditioned WT MscS inactivation more than G168D

evidence.explanation: Figures 4/6 and Discussion support adaptation and reversible DTT responses while leaving desensitization-versus-inactivation and structural chemistry unresolved.
Figure 4D/E, electrophysiology Methods and G168D Results support crowding-conditioned inactivation. Structural simulations, supplements and other gating contexts were not independently curated.

discussions.notes: Obtain complete clone sequences, per-panel host assignments, cited preparation protocols and independent bond/state measurements. The 2018 N117C/N167C lead is a different double mutant, not N117C/G168C. Other homologs and osmotic-survival phenotypes need separate evidence and domain mapping. Partial same-agent review does not promote this IN_PROGRESS entry to REVIEWED.

discussions.rationale: Channel-current perturbations establish functional coupling but do not directly demonstrate the proposed salt bridge, specific disulfide geometry or cage-motion pathway. The two studies use different state readouts and assay conditions.
